content.text: {"headline":"Recommended: no change for now (P0), and bring in the duty manager. Every plan that lifts service level breaks a policy rule, and doing nothing leaves us at a predicted 66%.","why":"The extra calls come from the 09:00 personal loan email (MKT-2026-551). Over the last four intervals there were 307 calls against 236 forecast, driven by loan_enquiry (92 vs 40) and new_offer_enquiry (50 vs 14). Staffing is on plan and there is no IT incident. Service level dropped to 68% at 09:45. With no action, the rest of the day is predicted at 66.3% (general 57.7%, payments 74.9%) with 7.2% abandons. P0 is the only option with no policy violations, so it was chosen by default. It does not reach the 80% target and is below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). The duty manager should be involved to decide whether a policy exception is justified.","trade_offs":["Policy decision for the duty manager: R2 (INR 6,000) gives 76.6% and R1 (INR 5,364) gives 75.7%. Both leave payments healthy (80.5% / 78.8%). Their only breach is BRK-04, with 2 agents having more than one break delayed. This is the mildest exception on the table.","P4 is the only plan that reaches target: 82.1% with 3.6% abandons for INR 3,780. It relies on a known-issue IVR message with no confirmed outage (CX-01), which misleads customers. Payments would also fall to 59% during the 11:00-13:00 move (MOV-03).","P3 (73.4%, INR 4,320) and P1 (66.1%, no cost) both pull payments below its 70% floor during the move (55% and 46%). P1 gains nothing overall.","P2 (78.9%, INR 108) is cheap but carries the same CX-01 and MOV-03 breaches as P4."],"watch":"Watch the general queue service level and abandons each interval. If loan and new-offer calls keep rising, ask marketing whether follow-up sends of MKT-2026-551 can be paused. Get the duty manager's decision on a BRK-04 exception (R1/R2) before 11:00, when the overtime and break-delay levers need to start."}
